# OmniConnect — The Bundle That Was Only Half Alive
> **GitHub-first narrative · GICS09 Communication Services · 2026-10-19.** Fictional architecture learning case. GitHub is canonical; Notion is the KM hub. New people, incidents and options are illustrative. Original research and14child references remain below. Unattended synchronization is unverified.
**Start here:** [Executive One-Pager](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/executive-one-pager.md) · [Hero Story](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/hero-story.md) · [22-Section Master](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/master/README.md) · [16 Personas](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md) · [12 Simulations](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/simulations/README.md) · [Seven Streams](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [Resources](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/resources/README.md)
## Prologue — A service with conflicting states
An invented converged bundle is billed active while connectivity and content entitlement are incomplete. Care, network and billing tools disagree. This prompts discovery, not a claim about a real outage or proven cause.
## Act I — Understand the Enterprise (OCN-M01–04)
Fictional CEO **Anika Rahman (OCN-P01)** leads a source-stipulated **USD37B** group with **62,000employees,28countries and210Mmobile/broadband/media subscriptions**, headquartered in Toronto/Dubai. Subscriptions do not necessarily equal unique people.
Mix:mobile34%, fixed/fiber25%, media19%, enterprise14%, advertising/data8%.
Source problems:fragmented domains, manual orchestration, identity/consent silos andtraffic-driven cost/energy pressure.
[Enterprise theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/master/theme-a-enterprise.md)
## Act II — Choose the Future (OCN-M05–08)
Convergence chief **Maya Patel (OCN-P03)** asks for simplicity; network chief **Arjun Mehta (OCN-P04)** requires operational authority; CFO **David Chen (OCN-P02)** challenges economics.
Compare domain-local pilots, central platform/network first and federated service experiments with common identity, catalog, privacy and resilience. Third option provisional.
NPS\>55,99.99%core availability,30%faster activation,20%higher engagement and18%lower cost remain undefined source ambitions.
[Strategy theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/master/theme-b-strategy.md)
## Act III — Architect Reconciled Services (OCN-M09–12)
Source chain: **Discover → Subscribe → Activate → Connect → Engage → Support → Retain**.
Fulfillment lead **Priya Shah (OCN-P13)** and architect **Daniel Weber (OCN-P12)** connect Subscriber/Service/Network/Content/Partner360, BSS/OSS/CRM/billing/CMS/ad-tech, API/event contracts and telemetry.
**Mei Lin (OCN-P09)** and **Omar Haddad (OCN-P10)** require consent, rights, permissions and recoverable boundaries. TM Forum/API/cloud-native patterns are source proposals, not conformance or production evidence.
[Architecture theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/master/theme-c-architecture.md)
## Act IV — Fund and Sequence Evidence (OCN-M13–16)
Source proposes **USD1.1B over3years** and **USD410M annual value**. Components, run cost, overlap, retention/revenue-to-margin, phasing and discounting absent; NPV/payback unvalidated.
Year1 identity, network data, core pilots → Year2 AI assurance, digital activation, converged offers → Year3 network APIs, edge and autonomous-operation proposals.
Targets:20%priority functions virtualized;25%faster fulfillment/15%fewer incidents;40%zero-touch/20%lower energy perTB.
[Transformation theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/master/theme-d-transformation.md)
## Act V — Make Change Usable and Recoverable (OCN-M17–19)
Assurance director **Marcus Okoro (OCN-P08)** asks whether subscribers actually recovered. CHRO **Nadia Fernandes (OCN-P07)** requires field/care learning and escalation support.
Illustrative first pilot uses synthetic data and simulated network actions. Test partial activation, identity/rights/consent, duplicates/late events, telemetry, reconciliation, stop/rollback and support. No production network action executed.
[Execution theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/master/theme-e-execution.md)
## Act VI — Prove Subscriber Value (OCN-M20–22)
Availability, activation, digital-care resolution, churn, engagement, energy perTB andAPI revenue need baselines, owners, cohorts and balancing measures.
**30%faster activation versus25%faster fulfillment** remains a scope/time/definition gap. Core availability differs from full experience; energy intensity differs from absolute energy. All future figures are targets, not results.
[Value theme](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/master/theme-f-value.md)
## Meet the Fictional Stakeholders
Anika Rahman—CEO; David Chen—CFO; Maya Patel—Convergence; Arjun Mehta—Network; Elena Brooks—Media; Sofia Tan—Digital/Information; Nadia Fernandes—CHRO; Marcus Okoro—Assurance; Mei Lin—Consent/Data; Omar Haddad—Security; Grace Menon—Enterprise/API; Daniel Weber—EA; Priya Shah—Fulfillment; Ravi Patel—Energy/FinOps; Amelia Jones—Subscriber/Client; Ingrid Sørensen—Partners/Procurement.
[Authority, objections and withheld evidence](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/personas/persona-cards.md)
## Practice and Derive
Twelve simulations cover discovery, activation, funding, closed loops, content/consent, skills, APIs, subscriber experience, AI, energy/partners, architecture and hypothetical STAR.
Seven blueprints cover Workforce/HR, CX, Finance, Procurement, Network/Service Operations, Business Transformation and Leadership.
**13HR child pages plus one Workforce Monday summary preserved**; child contents and implementations not audited. External media remain planned.
[Scripts](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/simulations/scenario-scripts.md) · [Streams](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/derived-streams/README.md) · [14 child references](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/references/notion-child-cases.md)
## Source and Synchronization Governance
Original research stays protected. Exact narrative maps to a GitHub baseline; conflicting edits are held. Other canonical changes need deliberate reconciliation; child pages and attachments are not losslessly mirrored.
[Sources/gaps](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/references/source-and-assumptions.md) · [Sync protocol](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/sync/README.md) · [Delivery report](https://github.com/nbnayak88/successlabs-case-studies/blob/main/09-communication-services/omniconnect-media-networks-ltd/delivery-report-2026-10-19.md)
**Delivery validation:** GitHub-to-Notion narrative was read back successfully. This note originated in Notion for the reverse-transfer test. OmniConnect is registered for daily reconciliation; unattended integration remains unverified.

# 🌟 GICS09. OmniConnect Media & Networks Ltd. — Business Transformation Case Study ## **Company Overview** **OmniConnect Media & Networks Ltd.** is a fictional multinational communication-services company operating telecom networks, broadband, streaming, news and entertainment platforms, advertising technology, and enterprise connectivity services. It is becoming a converged, digital-first connectivity and content ecosystem. --- ## **📊 Company Profile**
**Attribute** **Details**
**Founded** 1986
**Headquarters** Toronto, Canada & Dubai, UAE
**Global Presence** 28 countries
**Annual Revenue** \$37 billion USD
**Employees** 62,000 worldwide
**Subscribers** 210 million mobile, broadband, and media subscribers
### **Business Portfolio**
**Segment** **Revenue %** **Services**
Mobile & 5G Services 34% Consumer and enterprise mobile connectivity
Fixed Broadband & Fiber 25% Fiber, home Wi-Fi, business connectivity
Media & Streaming 19% Streaming, sports, news, original content
Enterprise Networks 14% SD-WAN, private 5G, cloud connectivity, IoT
Advertising & Data Services 8% Privacy-safe advertising and audience analytics
--- ## **🎯 Digital Transformation Vision** > *“Connecting people, organisations, and communities through trusted networks, relevant content, and intelligent digital experiences.”* ### **Transformation Drivers** 1. **Network Demand:** rising bandwidth, low-latency, and device-connectivity expectations. 2. **Convergence:** integrate mobile, fiber, Wi-Fi, content, and cloud services. 3. **Customer Experience:** simplify acquisition, service, and retention across channels. 4. **Content Economics:** increase engagement and monetisation while protecting trust. 5. **Network Efficiency:** automate operations and lower energy use per unit of traffic. --- # 🏗️ **TOGAF-Aligned Architecture Design** ## **Phase A: Architecture Vision** ### **Current-State Challenges** - Network, customer, billing, content, and advertising systems operate as separate domains. - Service activation and fault resolution involve manual orchestration across legacy stacks. - Personalisation is limited by consent, siloed identities, and inconsistent audience data. - Network energy use and operating costs increase as traffic and coverage expand. ### **Stakeholder Outcomes**
**Stakeholder** **Outcome** **Success Measure**
Subscribers Reliable, simple, relevant connectivity NPS \>55 and 99.99% core-network availability
Enterprise Clients Secure, programmable networks 30% faster service activation
Content Partners Engaged audiences and trusted monetisation 20% higher digital engagement
Investors Efficient growth and infrastructure return 18% operating-cost reduction
## **Phase B: Business Architecture** ```plain text CONNECTIVITY VALUE STREAM Discover → Subscribe → Activate → Connect → Engage → Support → Retain Future State: converged, personalised, self-healing connectivity and content services. ```
**Capability** **Target State** **Digital Enablers**
Network Operations Predictive and autonomous Network digital twin, AIOps, closed-loop automation
Service Fulfilment Instant, digital, zero-touch Catalog-driven orchestration and APIs
Audience Engagement Consent-based and relevant Customer data platform and recommendations
Enterprise Connectivity Programmable, secure, elastic Network APIs, edge cloud, private 5G
## **Phase C: Information Systems Architecture** ### **Data Architecture** ```plain text COMMUNICATIONS GOLDEN RECORDS Subscriber 360° → Service 360° → Network 360° → Content 360° → Partner 360° ``` - **Network data:** telemetry, capacity, topology, fault, energy, and service-quality events. - **Customer data:** consent, identity, subscriptions, interactions, device, and experience signals. - **Content data:** rights, metadata, audience engagement, advertising, and revenue metrics. - **Governance:** privacy, data minimisation, usage transparency, quality, and monetisation controls. ### **Target Application Landscape**
**Layer** **Core Systems** **Pattern**
Experience Subscriber app, self-service, streaming apps, enterprise portal Omni-channel and low-friction UX
Process BSS, OSS, CRM, billing, content management, ad-tech Domain-based service orchestration
Integration TM Forum APIs, event mesh, partner and network APIs Open, API-first interoperability
Data Telemetry lakehouse, CDP, network graph, content analytics Streaming and governed data products
## **Phase D: Technology Architecture** - **Cloud-native networks:** network functions, containers, edge services, and software-defined operations. - **Intelligent edge:** low-latency enterprise, IoT, content-delivery, and 5G services. - **Secure trust fabric:** zero trust, DDoS protection, fraud controls, privacy and content-rights protection. --- # 🤖 **AI & Advanced Analytics**
**Use Case** **Business Value** **Approach**
Network Assurance Fewer outages and faster recovery Telemetric anomaly detection and automated remediation
Churn Prevention Higher loyalty and retention Experience, usage, and service analytics
Content Recommendations Higher engagement and subscription value Consent-aware recommendation models
Field-Service Copilot Faster, safer maintenance work Grounded knowledge AI and visual assistance
--- # 📊 **3-Year Roadmap & Value Realisation**
**Phase** **Key Initiatives** **Success Metrics**
**Year 1 — Foundation** Unified identity, network-data platform, cloud-native core pilots 20% priority network functions virtualised
**Year 2 — Acceleration** AI assurance, digital service activation, converged offers 25% faster fulfilment; 15% fewer incidents
**Year 3 — Transformation** Programmable network APIs, edge ecosystem, autonomous operations 40% zero-touch fulfilment; 20% lower energy per TB
### **Investment & Outcomes** - **3-year investment:** \$1.1B in network modernisation, cloud platforms, security, data, and customer journeys. - **Expected benefits:** \$410M annual value from operating efficiency, customer retention, enterprise services, and content engagement. - **Core KPIs:** network availability, service-activation time, digital-care resolution, churn, engagement, energy per TB, and API revenue. --- # 🎉 **Conclusion** **OmniConnect Media & Networks Ltd.** becomes a converged, software-led connectivity ecosystem where trusted networks, relevant media, and programmable services reinforce one another. Its success requires open architecture, resilient operations, privacy-led engagement, and disciplined network modernisation. --- ## 14. Aligned business transformation case study blueprint ## Alignment purpose This section refines OmniConnect into the same business transformation case study structure used for OmniSpace while preserving the existing content. ### 14.1 Executive case narrative OmniConnect Media & Networks Ltd. is transforming from separate telecom, broadband, media, advertising, and enterprise-service domains into a converged, software-led connectivity and content ecosystem. **Core transformation statement:** OmniConnect is not only modernizing networks; it is building a governed transformation operating model where subscriber experience, network automation, content engagement, enterprise connectivity, privacy, APIs, and value realization work as one system. ### 14.2 Business problem statement
**Problem area** **Current challenge** **Transformation need**
Domain fragmentation Network, customer, billing, content, and advertising systems operate separately. Create Subscriber 360, Service 360, Network 360, Content 360, and Partner 360.
Manual service operations Activation, assurance, and fault resolution require manual orchestration. Implement catalog-driven fulfillment, AIOps, and closed-loop automation.
Convergence complexity Mobile, fiber, Wi-Fi, media, cloud, and enterprise services need unified experience. Build converged offers, unified identity, and common service orchestration.
Privacy and personalization Audience engagement depends on consent, identity, and trustworthy data use. Deploy privacy-safe CDP, consent governance, and responsible recommendations.
Network efficiency pressure Traffic growth increases cost, capacity, and energy requirements. Use network digital twins, energy analytics, and autonomous optimization.
### 14.3 Target transformation operating model ```plain text Business Outcomes ↓ Capability Architecture — Network, service, content, customer, enterprise connectivity ↓ Process Architecture — Discover, subscribe, activate, connect, engage, support, retain ↓ Data Architecture — Subscriber, service, network, content, partner golden records ↓ Application Architecture — BSS, OSS, CRM, billing, CMS, ad-tech ↓ Integration Architecture — TM Forum APIs, event mesh, partner and network APIs ↓ Technology Architecture — Cloud-native networks, edge, AIOps, programmable services ↓ Privacy, Resilience, Adoption, and Value Realization ``` **Operating rule:** Every connectivity workstream must connect network performance, subscriber experience, service orchestration, privacy, partner APIs, operational resilience, adoption, and business value. ### 14.4 Workstream alignment map
**Workstream** **Business outcome** **Architecture / process focus** **Delivery and adoption focus**
Network automation Fewer outages, faster recovery, lower operating cost. Network 360, telemetry, topology, fault events. AIOps, digital twin, closed-loop remediation.
Converged service experience Faster activation and simpler subscriber journeys. BSS/OSS, catalog, identity, billing, service orchestration. Self-service, zero-touch fulfillment, care tools.
Content and audience intelligence Higher engagement and trusted monetization. Content 360, consent, audience analytics, ad-tech. Recommendation models, privacy-safe advertising.
Programmable enterprise networks New enterprise revenue from secure network APIs. Network APIs, edge cloud, private 5G, partner governance. Developer portal, API marketplace, enterprise adoption.
### 14.5 Case study structure for publishing 1. **Situation** - OmniConnect operates mobile, fiber, broadband, media, streaming, advertising, and enterprise network services. 2. **Challenge** - It must unify experience, automate service operations, protect privacy, scale network capacity, and monetize programmable services. 3. **Transformation approach** - Use cloud-native networks, TM Forum APIs, AIOps, CDP, edge computing, privacy governance, and partner ecosystems. 4. **Execution model** - Build identity and data foundations, modernize network platforms, automate activation and assurance, and scale network APIs. 5. **Value realization** - Measure availability, activation time, incidents, churn, engagement, energy per TB, API revenue, and digital-care resolution. 6. **Long-term capability** - Build a repeatable converged connectivity transformation model across consumer, media, enterprise, and partner services. ### 14.6 Alignment rules - **Subscriber trust first:** Privacy, reliability, and clarity guide every experience. - **Network data as product:** Telemetry, topology, and service quality must be governed. - **Automation by design:** Fulfillment and assurance should move toward zero-touch. - **Open but controlled APIs:** Programmable networks require security and partner governance. - **Energy efficiency embedded:** Network growth must include sustainability metrics. - **Value after go-live:** Track operational and customer outcomes continuously. ### 14.7 Final aligned positioning ## Aligned case study positioning OmniConnect Media & Networks Ltd. demonstrates how communications transformation becomes measurable when network automation, converged services, content intelligence, privacy, programmable APIs, resilience, and value realization operate as one connected ecosystem.
